notes: Problem classes: every finding belongs to exactly one. A new instance of a known problem is an occurrence of its class, never a new class. A new class must state why it differs from EVERY existing class and carry an approval (docs/SELF_EVOLUTION.md). Questions are what `npm run brief` asks before a change; the commit gate requires answers to them.

classes.name: Absence read as success
classes.definition: Something a check needs is missing — an input, key, flag, file, field or piece of evidence — and the outcome reads as success or agreement instead of a refusal.

questions.ask: What happens when this input, key, file, flag or field is ABSENT? Absence must refuse or be declared — never read as success.
Delete it and run again: does the outcome still read PASS? If yes, the check is optional — make it required or declare why.

detectors: test/cli-strictness.test.mjs::every CLI refuses what it does not understand
test/bundle-absence.test.mjs::every silently deletable key is declared, and every declaration is still needed
test/ci-honesty.test.mjs::no workflow turns a skip or a failure into a green check
test/spend.test.mjs::chmod 000 on a log subdirectory is a typed deny, not $0
test/spend.test.mjs::chmod 000 on the log root PARENT is a typed deny, not "no logs"

classes.name: A partial fix or list stands in for the rule
classes.definition: A check, fix or list covers the instances someone thought of — one field, one file, one variable, one write site — instead of the rule they share, so the next instance passes.

questions.ask: Does a hand-written list stand in for 'all' (directories, keys, codes, fields, variables)? Enumerate from the source, or state the rule once and apply it everywhere.
You are fixing one instance: where else does the same rule apply, and does this change cover all of them?

detectors: test/bundle-absence.test.mjs::every silently deletable key is declared, and every declaration is still needed
test/claims-are-checked.test.mjs::each backticked file name in the docs appears in the code or the repository
eval/__tests__/exec-env.test.mjs::a failing suite stays red whatever NODE_OPTIONS or NODE_TEST_CONTEXT the operator has
test/self-evolution.test.mjs::the gate's files are listed once, and the list is what the checker loads (F-144)
test/guard.test.mjs::every wrapper, with a flag that takes a value, still names the command it runs (F-145)
test/secret-guard.test.mjs::K-SEC-049/K-SEC-050 a secret filename inside an upload reference, git path, copy or mount is denied
test/hook-scan-coverage.test.mjs::every tool and every payload field the hook can receive passes the same secret scan
test/hook-scan-coverage.test.mjs::the checklist covers every tool the installed matchers deliver (enumerated from the source)

stopline.detector: test/secret-guard.test.mjs::K-SEC-049/K-SEC-050 a secret filename inside an upload reference, git path, copy or mount is denied

classes.name: A check that cannot fail for the reason it names
classes.definition: A test, guard, fuzz or attack row passes for a reason other than the property it names: it never reaches the path, cannot take both values, proves a side effect, races nothing, or has no control.

questions.ask: Does the check fail for the reason it names, and only that? Put the bug back and watch it go red.
Can this test actually observe what its name claims — does the race overlap, does the attack reach a live target? Add the control that proves it.
Can this check fail when the thing it guards is not done — not just when its paperwork is missing? Tie the record to something that resolves or runs.

detectors: test/core-specs.test.mjs::each red line in docs/testing-profile.md names a drill anchor that exists
test/claims-are-checked.test.mjs::every refusal code a source can emit is asserted by at least one test
eval/__tests__/scorer-rules.test.mjs::fires on its trigger, and not without it
test/ledger-archive.test.mjs::verify catches a lost index, and reserve refuses rather than re-admit a sealed call-id
test/bounded-spawn.test.mjs::every node --test run loads the bound, whatever flags come first (F-215)

classes.name: Unbounded or clock-judged cost
classes.definition: Time, size or work is unbounded on attacker- or load-shaped input, or a test judges it with a wall clock.

questions.ask: What bounds the work, time or size here on hostile input — and is that bound asserted by a counter or a refusal, not a stopwatch?

detectors: test/claims-are-checked.test.mjs::no test or check script asserts speed with a tight wall clock
test/claims-are-checked.test.mjs::every node --test script carries --test-timeout
test/cost-bounds.test.mjs::every exported function shows how its work is bounded
test/bounded-spawn.test.mjs::every node --test run loads the bound
test/ledger-archive.test.mjs::per-call work stays flat as history grows (operation count, not a clock)

stopline.detector: test/cost-bounds.test.mjs::every exported function shows how its work is bounded

classes.name: A statement the code does not keep
classes.definition: A sentence in docs, specs, packs, README, CHANGELOG or the tool's own status output states behaviour, coverage, a file or a figure the code does not have.

questions.ask: Is every sentence you add to docs, specs or packs backed by a test that fails without it? Read it back against the code, not the intent.
Does every figure or exit code the tool reports work when someone acts on it?

detectors: test/claims-are-checked.test.mjs::every code the user-facing docs name exists in the code
test/claims-are-checked.test.mjs::each backticked file name in the docs appears in the code or the repository
test/claims-are-checked.test.mjs::no user-facing text calls a record signed, immutable or tamper-proof without a mechanism
test/guard.test.mjs::the spec lists the shipped rules in their order, with their answers (F-148)

classes.name: Weak evidence presented as strong
classes.definition: Evidence from a weaker source — a FAKE run, a stub binary, a modified tree, a self-shipped verifier, an agent-writable record — is presented as if it came from the stronger one.

questions.ask: Which source does this evidence really come from, and does every reader see that source — not a stronger one?

detectors: eval/__tests__/case-packs.test.mjs::FAKE mode → HARNESS_ONLY for every requirement, even when every case passed
test/evidence-bundle.test.mjs::a REAL run whose metrics name no model → METRICS_UNVERIFIABLE, even with traces relabelled

classes.name: Untrusted input trusted
classes.definition: Input or state controlled by someone else — caller ids, operator text, agent arguments, repository state, files on disk — crosses into the code without validation, escaping or isolation.

questions.ask: Which inputs come from someone else — the agent under test, operator text, hand-edited files, repository state? Each crosses a trust boundary: validate, escape, or do not trust it.
Can the party this gate constrains perform the step that clears it? A person must.

detectors: test/hostile-names.test.mjs::callIds and agentIds that are prototype names reserve, settle, halt and resume like any id
test/mcp.test.mjs::F-82: hostile frame shapes answer an error and the gate keeps serving
test/spend.test.mjs::a line stamped tomorrow lands in today, flagged, and still hits the cap

stopline.detector: test/spend.test.mjs::a line stamped tomorrow lands in today, flagged, and still hits the cap

classes.name: One thing, two names
classes.definition: The same resource is reachable under two names — symlink, hard link, relative path, case alias, an enclosing repository — and the code treats them as different, or one as the other.

questions.ask: Can the same thing be reached by two names (symlink, hard link, relative path, case alias, enclosing repository)? One name must be the only one.

detectors: test/ledger.test.mjs::F-85: a ledger reached through a symlinked or hard-linked FILE refuses
eval/__tests__/stranger-regressions.test.mjs::relative --out stranger
test/guard.test.mjs::a delete that takes the repository, the home folder or Sakk state with it is denied before any allow (F-146)
test/guard.test.mjs::a guard-state, outside-repo or destructive-git target held in a shell variable or brace is asked, never allowed (F-176)

stopline.detector: test/guard.test.mjs::a guard-state, outside-repo or destructive-git target held in a shell variable or brace is asked, never allowed (F-176)

classes.name: An environment or state assumed, never tried
classes.definition: The code assumes an environment, layout or reachable state — PATH and node location, git version or config, which git operations run hooks, which states a genuine run reaches — that was never tested in its other form.

questions.ask: Which environment or state does this assume — repository top, PATH node, git config, which operations run hooks, which states a real run reaches? Test the other one.
Where will this really run — which folder the session starts in, which agent, which loader? Show it firing there, not only that it is configured.

detectors: eval/__tests__/stranger-regressions.test.mjs::relative --out stranger
test/secret-scan.test.mjs::the hook as SHIPPED
test/core-specs.test.mjs::every drill entry is recognised, however many letters its id has (F-147)
test/range-topology.test.mjs::a stack merged into main as one pull request: the parents' answers files are inherited, not carried forward
test/pre-push.test.mjs::a push from a linked worktree: the suite gets no GIT_ variables, so a fixture cannot write into the repository (F-214)
test/claims-are-checked.test.mjs::every node --test launch in package.json and the hooks loads test/clean-git-env.mjs first

classes.name: A required step exists only as rule text
classes.definition: A step the process requires — a spec, a drill anchor, a lint, a gate, a version bump, a release roll, a campaign run — exists only as written rule and gets skipped.

questions.ask: Is a required step enforced only by rule text? Make the gate, a hook or the audit run it, and make a test fail when it is missing.

Can the step be skipped by another route — another tool, another agent, a session started elsewhere, or by changing its input after the gate passed? Make every route meet the gate, and freeze what it read.

detectors: test/claims-are-checked.test.mjs::the commit gate passes exit codes straight through
test/core-specs.test.mjs::every source file is classified core or not core
test/core-specs.test.mjs::each script in scripts/campaign/ is a step of the audit
test/core-specs.test.mjs::every drill anchor is found exactly once in its file, without running the drill (F-149)
test/pre-push.test.mjs::a push runs the range check and the full suite, and refuses when either fails

classes.name: A value whose meaning outlives its scope
classes.definition: A write or value carries a meaning beyond what its writer did — a timestamp that means 'confirmed', a lock that a manual override bypasses.

questions.ask: Does this write or value carry a meaning beyond its scope, and who can cause it? Classify every writer by what it confirms and who calls it.

detectors: test/kill-switch.test.mjs::each writeLedger call sits in a classified function, with the matching option
test/kill-switch.test.mjs::resume with nothing halted never enters the write path (F-209)

classes.name: Judged on the literal without its context
classes.definition: A rule decides on the captured text alone, without what surrounds it or what the capture swallowed.

questions.ask: Is a match judged on the captured text alone? Judge it in context: what surrounds it, and what the capture swallowed.

detectors: test/secret-scan.test.mjs::RC-03 class: a fiction token beside any real secret, in any position, never hides it

classes.name: A detector tuned on one side
classes.definition: A detection rule misses real instances or flags ordinary ones, because it was tuned on positive or negative samples only.

questions.ask: Has this detection rule been measured on both sides — real instances it must catch and ordinary inputs it must leave alone?

detectors: test/secret-scan.test.mjs::ordinary identifiers starting sk_/rk_/sk- are not API keys

classes.name: The real path never exercised
classes.definition: Tests and stand-ins exercise a different path from the one the product runs — fake agents writing their own evidence, amounts that never overrun, fixtures the real executor never sees.

questions.ask: Does any test run the real path — the real executor, the real fixture, the overrun — or only a stand-in that writes its own evidence?

classes.name: The judge is the writer
classes.definition: The same model or person that wrote a change also judged it, with no measured bias.

questions.ask: Was the judge different from the writer (another model, a fresh clone)?
